# Retired claims

*Generated by `scripts/claims.py` from the claims register. Each passage below is read out of this repository's history at the commit named, so it is what the site actually published, not a paraphrase.*

A claim is retired when no good justification for it can be given - most often because its justification was never recorded properly. It is not quietly deleted: it is kept here, in its own words, with the reason, and the page that made it now says only what can be justified. Nothing on this page is claimed to be true. What is claimed is that the site once said it.

## AREAS.md

<a id="C-AR-OLD-AGG"></a>
### Every number in the national argument is an aggregate, including a percentage rule, and a figure true of Denmark is true of nowhere in it.

`C-AR-OLD-AGG` · retired 2026-09-11 from [AREAS.md](AREAS.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-OLD-AGG">Every number in the national argument is an aggregate: one land-borne load, one [69.6](SOURCES.md#F-767dbaca2d)%, one ladder of indsatsbehov, one [25](SOURCES.md#F-d9deee2e38)% rule. Aggregation is where the information goes. Køge Bugt and Ringkøbing Fjord do not share a cause, a flushing time, a sediment, or a fix, and a figure true of Denmark is true of nowhere in it</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-AR-OLD-AGG "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** The percentage rule it named has no source anywhere in the repository; its justification was not recorded properly. 'Every number' and 'true of nowhere' overgeneralise: a national figure need not hold in any one water body, which is what the replacement says.

**Replaced by:** [`C-AR-AGG`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-AGG) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-AR-OLD-CAUTION"></a>
### An earlier claim about what the water bodies encode was backwards, and survived until a second control was computed.

`C-AR-OLD-CAUTION` · retired 2026-09-11 from [AREAS.md](AREAS.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-OLD-CAUTION">A correction, and the reason this section is written as a caution. An earlier version said the water bodies "encode salinity strongly and oxygen almost not at all", from the shuffled control alone. Against a null matching both size and shape that is backwards. The claim was defensible, reproducible, and wrong — and it survived exactly as long as it took to compute a second control. Any single number here would have been publishable; the disagreement between the nulls is the finding</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-AR-OLD-CAUTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** History the reader does not need; the replacement states the finding - the nulls disagree - without it.

**Replaced by:** [`C-AR-THREE-RANKINGS`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-THREE-RANKINGS) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-AR-OLD-ICC"></a>
### The partition score is the intraclass correlation, on which zero means membership tells nothing.

`C-AR-OLD-ICC` · retired 2026-09-11 from [AREAS.md](AREAS.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-OLD-ICC">So the question is what the water bodies encode, and the statistic is the intraclass correlation computed within month: pick two stations at random in the same month — if they are in the same water body, how much more alike are they than two picked without regard to it? One means membership tells you everything; zero means it tells you nothing beyond the season</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-AR-OLD-ICC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** The statistic computed is the mean-square ratio MSB/(MSB+MSW), on which labels carrying no information score near one half; read as an intraclass correlation, every value in the table overstates what membership tells.

**Replaced by:** [`C-AR-PART-STAT`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-PART-STAT) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-AR-OLD-CLOTHES"></a>
### Citizenship, race, species, sector, diagnosis codes and postcodes each show the membership-attribution split, with stated figures and history.

`C-AR-OLD-CLOTHES` · retired 2026-09-11 from [CATEGORY.md](CATEGORY.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AR-OLD-CLOTHES">Not rare, and not Danish. One line each, with no claim that any is wrong — only that each has a membership rule doing one job and an attribution doing another: - Citizenship. A determinate legal status, acquired by birth, descent or naturalisation. Used as a proxy for population, culture, ancestry, or behaviour — none of which the membership rule tracks. The rule is *legal*; the attribution is usually *biological or cultural*. - Race. The literature's central dispute is exactly this statistic. Lewontin (1972) partitioned human genetic variance: ~[85](SOURCES.md#F-01d1e0e572)% within populations, ~[15](SOURCES.md#F-29bd7fbbc0)% between — an ICC of [0.15](SOURCES.md#F-7cc7eeb760). Edwards (2003) replied that correlated loci make classification accurate anyway, which is true and is *our compact-null finding*: high classifiability is what a smooth cline gives you wherever you cut it. Rosenberg et al. (2002) is cited for finding clusters; Serre & Pääbo (2004) sampled the same geography continuously and got gradients. Sampling design, again. - Species. Biological, morphological and phylogenetic species concepts are three different membership rules over the same organisms, and they do not agree. Which one is "correct" has no answer; which one predicts a given trait does. - Industrial sector (SIC, NACE). A firm's code is assigned, often by the firm. Productivity and emissions are then compared "within sector". - Diagnosis codes. A membership rule built for billing, used as a phenotype. - Deprivation by postcode. An area statistic attributed to the individuals in it — which is the ecological fallacy, and the same error AREAS.md reports for Denmark</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-AR-OLD-CLOTHES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Several parts had nothing behind them or went beyond their sources: the race figures were typed without a source, 'the literature's central dispute' overstated, Serre and Pääbo sampled homogeneously across the globe rather than 'the same geography continuously', the species review proposes a unified concept where the page said 'no answer', diagnosis codes were built for statistics rather than billing, and 'often by the firm' was unchecked.

**Replaced by:** [`C-AR-CITIZENSHIP`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-CITIZENSHIP), [`C-AR-RACE`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-RACE), [`C-AR-SPECIES`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SPECIES), [`C-AR-SECTOR`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-SECTOR), [`C-AR-ICD`](CLAIMS.md#C-AR-ICD) — each opens what it rests on.

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-NOISE-CONSTRUCTION">The estimate is now taken only from cells whose samples all fall in one sun-elevation bin, where no diurnal variance can enter by construction.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-NOISE-CONSTRUCTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Overstated, and the method has changed since: the noise now comes from samples whose moving-window neighbours share their sun bin, not from fixed cells, and a bin spans a range of sun elevations, so diurnal variation inside one bin can still enter.

**Replaced by:** [`C-ML-NOISE-NOW`](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-NOW) — each opens what it rests on.

### The first noise estimate was asserted, and the second was a within-cell residual that contained the signal.

`C-ML-OLD-NOISE-HISTORY` · retired 2026-09-11 from [METHOD_LAB.md](METHOD_LAB.md) · as published in `eb2d0a2`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-NOISE-HISTORY">version asserted [0.8](SOURCES.md#F-fab5de42bc) mg/l, which made the bound only as good as a guess. The second measured the archive's within-cell residual spread - and that residual *contains whatever diurnal signal exists*, so a large real cycle would have inflated the yardstick used to rule a large real cycle out.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-NOISE-HISTORY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** About this project's own past and not needed to read the method: the reader needs the hazard, which the replacement states. Its only record is the comment detectable.py carried when it was first committed; the first two versions were never committed.

**Replaced by:** [`C-ML-NOISE-CIRC`](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-CIRC) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-ML-OLD-NOISE-SCALES"></a>
### The detection limit scales with the noise estimate.

`C-ML-OLD-NOISE-SCALES` · retired 2026-09-11 from [METHOD_LAB.md](METHOD_LAB.md) · as published in `eb2d0a2`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-NOISE-SCALES">The detection limit above scales with an estimate of the noise an estimator must see through.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-NOISE-SCALES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** The bound is not proportional to the noise estimate: more noise raises the draws' median and widens their scatter, which push in opposite directions, and no stored run shows the net. What can be justified is that the bound depends on it.

**Replaced by:** [`C-ML-NOISE-CIRC`](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-CIRC) — each opens what it rests on.

`C-ML-OLD-SCHEDULE` · retired 2026-09-11 from [METHOD_LAB.md](METHOD_LAB.md) · as published in `eb2d0a2`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-SCHEDULE">`scripts/detectable.py` takes the [91,093](SOURCES.md#F-f97885da46) real surface-oxygen visits in the water-chemistry extract - their true stations, dates and clock times - imposes a diurnal cycle of stipulated amplitude keyed to the sun's elevation, and runs the same estimator OPEN_PROBLEMS.md item 17 uses on the real data. It claims nothing about how the sea behaves. It asks only: *if it behaved this way, at this amplitude, would this schedule have found out?</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-SCHEDULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<a id="C-ML-OLD-SETTLES"></a>
### The simulation settles what OPEN_PROBLEMS.md had asserted without evidence: that the working-hours window is why the pre-dawn minimum is invisible.

`C-ML-OLD-SETTLES` · retired 2026-09-11 from [METHOD_LAB.md](METHOD_LAB.md) · as published in `eb2d0a2`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-SETTLES">It also settles something that had been asserted without evidence. OPEN_PROBLEMS.md said the 09:00-15:00 window is *why* the pre-dawn minimum is invisible. That was a plausible story. It is now a measured attenuation with a number on it</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-SETTLES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** The earlier statement rested on a count of how few samples fall at night or in twilight, so it was not without evidence; and what the simulation measures is the loss of a whole sun-shaped cycle's contrast, not the visibility of the pre-dawn minimum. The current result does not need this history.

**Not replaced** — nothing that could be justified was found to say in its place.

<a id="C-ML-OLD-SINGLEBIN"></a>
### Almost every station-window cell holds samples from one sun bin, and that explains the working day's attenuation mechanically.

`C-ML-OLD-SINGLEBIN` · retired 2026-09-11 from [METHOD_LAB.md](METHOD_LAB.md) · as published in `eb2d0a2`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-SINGLEBIN">And the reason it cannot be seen at all Fixing the circularity produced a diagnostic worth more than the fix. Of [81,627](SOURCES.md#F-6042bd2a1f) station-window cells, [80,445](SOURCES.md#F-a5f38c7915) - [98.5](SOURCES.md#F-db7c8b689f)% - contain samples from only one sun-elevation bin. Within a station's own ten-day window, the water is almost always sampled at the same height of sun. That is a harder limit than a narrow working day. A fixed-effects estimator sees a diurnal signal only through *within-cell* contrast, and [98.5](SOURCES.md#F-db7c8b689f)% of the cells have none to offer. Whatever the archive can say about the daily cycle rests on the remaining [1.5](SOURCES.md#F-897b340ba5)%. It also explains the three-quarters attenuation above mechanically rather than by analogy: the hours are not merely narrow, they are repeated</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-SINGLEBIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Counted in fixed cells, with the clock read as UTC and filled-in defaults included, and which of these produced the count was never separated; the mechanical explanation of the attenuation rested on it. The replacement counts samples over the estimator's own window, on observed instants only, and draws no causal link.

**Replaced by:** [`C-ML-NEIGHBOURS`](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NEIGHBOURS) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-NI-OLD-PASSTHROUGH"></a>
### Per catchment, only a small fraction of the fall in field surplus reached the measured diffuse load, and none in one catchment.

`C-NI-OLD-PASSTHROUGH` · retired 2026-09-11 from [NITROGEN.md](NITROGEN.md) · as published in `1bccd8b`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-NI-OLD-PASSTHROUGH">So how does the construction perform against things that were measured? This is the question the rest of it turns on, and Windolf et al. (2012) answer it per catchment. Over 1990–2009: | catchment | field surplus fell | measured normalised diffuse load fell | pass-through | |---|---|---|---| | Horsens, Isefjord, Odense | [30](SOURCES.md#F-c3df613f69)–[52](SOURCES.md#F-032b75dbb7) kg N ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ | [10](SOURCES.md#F-c9cfdb1949)–[14](SOURCES.md#F-08aca8328a) | roughly ¼ to ⅓ | | Randers, Roskilde | [24](SOURCES.md#F-d78b9a678b)–[50](SOURCES.md#F-667e53d061) | [3](SOURCES.md#F-875ec555b1)–[5](SOURCES.md#F-d6d42db3ae) | roughly a tenth | | Mariager | fell as elsewhere | no response traceable | zero | The construction moves and the measurement mostly does not. For every kilogram per hectare the surplus fell, the measured diffuse load fell by something like [0.1](SOURCES.md#F-3f3cfc72d0) to [0.4](SOURCES.md#F-76c2fc7c57) where it responded at all, and by nothing in one catchment of ten. The paper attributes the spread to nitrogen removal in groundwater varying with geology, and the Mariager failure to old oxic aquifers where nitrate survives. Read carefully, that is three separate findings: [1](SOURCES.md#F-88806f41dc). Direction: good. Nine of ten catchments show a significant relation. The surplus is not noise. [2](SOURCES.md#F-5830449f6a). Magnitude: poor. The transfer coefficient ranges from [0](SOURCES.md#F-3d678516bf) to about a third. A load reduction predicted from a surplus reduction would be overestimated by a factor of three to ten, or entirely, depending which catchment you are standing in. [3](SOURCES.md#F-875ec555b1). And the national figure hides exactly this. Figur 6.7 D shows *"en meget stærk, signifikant lineær relation"* at national scale. That relation is an aggregate over catchments whose individual pass-through runs from zero to a third. The strength of the national fit is not evidence that the local coefficient is stable — it is what aggregation does to a variable coefficient. Point [3](SOURCES.md#F-875ec555b1) is this project's recurring finding arriving in the nitrogen account: a basket looks tight from outside and is heterogeneous within, and the tightness is partly an artefact of looking from outside. It is the same shape as the water bodies that carry no within-basket signal, and the same shape as a national trend that tracks which stations were reporting. None of which says the decline was not real. Measured estuary nitrogen fell [24](SOURCES.md#F-d78b9a678b)–[62](SOURCES.md#F-28be7562da)% and measured inlet concentrations [18](SOURCES.md#F-8fbcba9699)–[55](SOURCES.md#F-2def35cbcf)%. Something large happened. What the numbers do not support is using the surplus as a quantitative instrument — sizing an intervention on it, or converting a surplus target into an expected load</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-NI-OLD-PASSTHROUGH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Its justification was not recorded properly: the paper is paywalled, the one open copy listed for it has been withdrawn, and nothing the site stored holds its figures, so no one can check them here.

**Replaced by:** [`C-NI-PERFORMANCE-UNREAD`](CLAIMS.md#C-NI-PERFORMANCE-UNREAD) — each opens what it rests on.

`C-NI-OLD-REFUTED` · retired 2026-09-11 from [NITROGEN.md](NITROGEN.md) · as published in `1bccd8b`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-NI-OLD-REFUTED">But two things in this paper are not circular at all, and together they carry the attribution: [1](SOURCES.md#F-7609f435b4). Stream and upper-estuary concentrations *"nearly halved over the time frame investigated."* [2](SOURCES.md#F-afc61f51c9). The catchments respond differently, and that is the tell. Eight show a direct response under five years; two show a decadal delay attributed to nitrate surviving in oxic chalk aquifers. The broad claim — that the attribution lacks independent support — is now positively refuted, not merely unestablished. Measured stream loads over a gauged majority, measured estuary concentrations, and between-catchment heterogeneity are support that no circularity in one monitoring-report figure touches</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-NI-OLD-REFUTED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<a id="C-NI-OLD-SETTLED"></a>
### Reading the paper settled the question against this project's first draft.

`C-NI-OLD-SETTLED` · retired 2026-09-11 from [NITROGEN.md](NITROGEN.md) · as published in `1bccd8b`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-NI-OLD-SETTLED">This is worth stating plainly because it is the error this project audits, committed here twice in one hour, in both directions. First we found one bad argument and let it stand for the case — a bad argument in a source does not mean there are no good ones. Then, correcting that, we asserted from a *title* that a non-circular design existed. Softening an overclaim is still an overclaim. Reading the paper settled it, and against us. That is the steelman rule working as intended: the strongest version of the case was looked for, found, and turned out to be stronger than the finding. The circularity is real and local. The attribution is not unevidenced. Both sentences are needed, and only the first was in the first draft</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-NI-OLD-SETTLED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** About this project's own drafting rather than the nitrogen account, and 'reading the paper settled it' cannot stand when the paper cannot be read here.

<a id="C-NI-OLD-WINDOLF-READ"></a>
### A catchment-and-estuary study was read, and its design and gauged shares showed where the relation is circular.

`C-NI-OLD-WINDOLF-READ` · retired 2026-09-11 from [NITROGEN.md](NITROGEN.md) · as published in `1bccd8b`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-NI-OLD-WINDOLF-READ">We have now read it, and it refutes the broader reading. Windolf, Blicher-Mathiesen, Carstensen & Kronvang (2012), *Environmental Science and Policy* 24: 24–33, 10.1016/j.envsci.2012.08.009. The design is a catchment↔estuary pairing — [10](SOURCES.md#F-344f281055) catchments covering [35](SOURCES.md#F-5d72913c63)% of Danish land area with their estuaries, 1990–2009 — not the treated-versus-control paired catchment experiment. On that, an earlier draft of this section guessed right and then guessed wrong about what followed. What matters is where the numbers come from: | link | how it is obtained | |---|---| | catchment N surplus | the norm-product residual, as above | | stream N load | measured on the gauged fraction — fortnightly total-N concentrations × daily discharge — and modelled on the rest per Windolf et al. (2011), the DK-QNP family | | estuary total N | measured. Discrete samples, surface and bottom, [12](SOURCES.md#F-6242ae8623)–[46](SOURCES.md#F-957d390c97)×/year, upper/middle/lower reaches | Gauged area runs from [22](SOURCES.md#F-d60c250c7d)% (Isefjord) to [87](SOURCES.md#F-527a0d0ab7)% (Randers Fjord), median about [66](SOURCES.md#F-bb25fd57c1)%. So the surplus↔load relation *is* partly circular, and unevenly so — at Isefjord more than three quarters of the catchment is modelled, at Randers about an eighth</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-NI-OLD-WINDOLF-READ "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Its justification was not recorded properly: the paper is paywalled, the one open copy listed for it has been withdrawn, and nothing the site stored holds its figures, so no one can check them here.

**Replaced by:** [`C-NI-WINDOLF-UNREAD`](CLAIMS.md#C-NI-WINDOLF-UNREAD) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-ML-OLD-EXACT-DESIGN"></a>
### DCE's variable selection is an exhaustive best-subset search, and simulating that search on pure noise reproduces their design exactly.

`C-ML-OLD-EXACT-DESIGN` · retired 2026-09-11 from [OBSERVING.md](OBSERVING.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OLD-EXACT-DESIGN">That is a best-subset search over [92](SOURCES.md#F-f1a292a8cb) candidate models fitted to about [20](SOURCES.md#F-b82a69c091) points. So the question is not whether R² = [0.57](SOURCES.md#F-4917c11a07) is high. It is what that search returns when there is no relation there at all. Simulating exactly their design</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-ML-OLD-EXACT-DESIGN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Not what the report describes: DCE select stepwise on cross-validated error, offer each candidate over many period windows, hold out a validation set and accept on several criteria. The simulation runs a simpler, exhaustive in-sample search.

`C-OB-OLD-BUILTTOSEE` · retired 2026-09-11 from [OBSERVING.md](OBSERVING.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OB-OLD-BUILTTOSEE">What the observing system is actually built to see Set the two records side by side. Denmark's densest, longest, most replicated marine observation is of faecal contamination — is it safe to swim. The chain policy acts on — nitrogen to algae to oxygen to a dead seabed — is observed far more thinly, and the oxygen end of it most thinly of all. | | stations | water bodies | years | data points entering the analysis | |---|---:|---:|---|---:| | Bathing water (faecal indicator) | [728](SOURCES.md#F-fb57b0d964) | [70](SOURCES.md#F-fb3c0f06b7) | 1991–2018 | [19,714](SOURCES.md#F-9b35801653) station-years | | Nutrient/chlorophyll/Kd models | [29](SOURCES.md#F-712aa88a79) | [22](SOURCES.md#F-9bfdbf51b5) | 1990–2012 | ~[1,440](SOURCES.md#F-490af1b220) seasonal means ([72](SOURCES.md#F-978cc3647b) models × ≥[15](SOURCES.md#F-86d3553025) points) | | Oxygen indicator | — | per water body | rolling [6](SOURCES.md#F-69567d4867)-year | [1](SOURCES.md#F-1506f2123e) value per water body per [6](SOURCES.md#F-69567d4867) years | Roughly fourteen times as many observations stand behind the faecal record as behind every nutrient model in the country combined, they are spread over three times as many water bodies, and they run thirteen years further forward — through exactly the period the fitted window excludes. That is not a small technical asymmetry. It means the sewage pathway is the one Denmark can actually measure, and the nutrient pathway is the one Denmark acts on. The two hypotheses about what wrecks a Danish shore are not being weighed against each other on comparable evidence — one has an observing system and the other has a model.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-OB-OLD-BUILTTOSEE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<a id="C-OB-OLD-LIST-GAPS"></a>

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OB-OLD-LIST-GAPS">That list is worth reading for what is not on it. An oxygen deficit is a balance — what removes oxygen against what resupplies it — and the routes on both sides are many. Imported organic matter exerts its demand directly, with no nitrogen and no growth step in between. Ammonium exerts a demand chemically, by being oxidised. Sulphide released from disturbed sediment consumes oxygen the moment it meets it. A kill event of any cause leaves a decaying mass and a bacterial bloom on it. Warmer water holds less; a column that does not turn over does not refill. None of those is a candidate variable, so whatever share belongs to them has nowhere to go but into the coefficients on the variables that are there.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-OB-OLD-LIST-GAPS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<a id="C-OB-OLD-SIGNATURE"></a>
### DCE report the TN models' drift without drawing the inference, and the drift is the signature of a missing covariate.

`C-OB-OLD-SIGNATURE` · retired 2026-09-11 from [OBSERVING.md](OBSERVING.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OB-OLD-SIGNATURE">DCE report the symptom without drawing the inference: > *"TN-modellerne har generelt en tendens til systematiske afvigelser over tid, idet de høje TN-koncentrationer observeret i starten af 1990'erne underestimeres, mens de lave TN-koncentrationer i sidste del af perioden overestimeres."* A predicted range compressed against a monotone observed trend is the signature of a missing monotone covariate. Their own explanation names one and leaves it out of the model: *"tidsforsinkelsen pga. ophobning af organisk bundet kvælstof i sedimenterne"* - an unmodelled state variable with memory.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-OB-OLD-SIGNATURE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** DCE do draw an inference - they attribute the difference to the time lag of nitrogen accumulating in the sediments; the quotation's wording did not match the report; and a compressed range is one thing a missing trending variable would produce, not a signature only it leaves.

**Replaced by:** [`C-OB-DCE-TNDRIFT`](CLAIMS.md#C-OB-DCE-TNDRIFT), [`C-OB-MISSING-COVARIATE`](CLAIMS.md#C-OB-MISSING-COVARIATE) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-OB-OLD-OX-CELLS"></a>

`C-OB-OLD-OX-CELLS` · retired 2026-09-11 from [OXYGEN.md](OXYGEN.md) · as published in `0739c86`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OB-OLD-OX-CELLS">Common in fjords with an annual cycle. | no — an oxygen trigger fires either way | | ● | ○ | ● | Nitrogen present, water well oxygenated, fauna gone anyway: toxicants, antifoulants, pharmaceutical residues, ammonia toxicity, or physical destruction by trawling and dredging. Oxygen is not the only way to kill. | no | | ● | ○ | ○ | A loaded but well-flushed system. Køge Bugt's flushing time is [73](SOURCES.md#F-419f6468ac) days; the Limfjord broads are far longer. The same load in the two places is not the same pressure, and the load term does not know which it is in. | no | | ○ | ● | ● | Oxygen consumed by material that arrived already made — the toilet-flush case — or by sulphide from disturbed sediment, or by decay after a kill of another cause. No nitrogen needed at any step. | no | | ○ | ● | ○ | A naturally anoxic or hypoxic basin with its own community. Deep sills, the Black Sea below [150](SOURCES.md#F-cd90c4ad00) m, the millimetre beneath any marine sediment surface.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-OB-OLD-OX-CELLS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<a id="C-OB-OLD-OX-CORRECTION"></a>
### An earlier version generalised one layer's sediment count to Denmark, and ICES DOME holds a longer record this project has not verified.

`C-OB-OLD-OX-CORRECTION` · retired 2026-09-11 from [OXYGEN.md](OXYGEN.md) · as published in `0739c86`

That generalised one layer — the VP3 hazardous-substance stations — to the whole country, and it was wrong on both counts. The count in that layer is five, and a separate international archive (ICES DOME) holds a longer Danish marine sediment record that this project has not yet verified for itself. The defensible claim is narrower: the national water-plan monitoring that feeds the assessment looks at biota and water and almost never at the bed, which is a statement about what the assessment can see rather than about what exists somewhere.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-OB-OLD-OX-CORRECTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<a id="C-OB-OLD-OX-DENSEST"></a>
### The anoxic sediment layer is among the densest microbial habitats on the planet, with white bacterial mats, a permanently anoxic Black Sea below a stated depth, and nematodes increasing because their predators left.

`C-OB-OLD-OX-DENSEST` · retired 2026-09-11 from [OXYGEN.md](OXYGEN.md) · as published in `0739c86`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OB-OLD-OX-DENSEST">Marine sediment goes anoxic within millimetres of its surface, and that anoxic layer is among the densest microbial habitats on the planet. Sulphide-oxidising bacterial mats — *Beggiatoa*, *Thioploca* — form thick white sheets exactly where oxygen is nearly absent and sulphide is plentiful; they are a *feature* of hypoxic beds, not an absence of life. The Black Sea below about [150](SOURCES.md#F-c40f437ca3) m has been permanently anoxic throughout recorded history and holds an active microbial community throughout. Hypoxia-tolerant nematodes and foraminifera frequently *increase* in abundance under low oxygen, because the things that ate them and competed with them are the things that left.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-OB-OLD-OX-DENSEST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Several pieces had no source: densest on the planet, the colour of the mats, the Black Sea's depth and permanence, and the reason nematodes and foraminifera are favoured. What the pinned review supports is kept.

**Replaced by:** [`C-OB-OX-LOWLIFE`](CLAIMS.md#C-OB-OX-LOWLIFE) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-PG-OLD-ECOLABEL"></a>
### The Nordic Swan and Den Blå Krans restrict legal substances and have a large market, which is evidence the legal floor is too low.

`C-PG-OLD-ECOLABEL` · retired 2026-09-11 from [PROGRAMME.md](PROGRAMME.md) · as published in `7954022`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PG-OLD-ECOLABEL">There is a straightforward test of whether a regulatory floor matches what people actually want, and Denmark runs it continuously. Svanemærket — the Nordic Swan — is a lifecycle ecolabel with criteria set by a Nordic board, verified by third parties, tightened on a cycle, and awarded only to the better performers in a product category. Astma-Allergi Danmark's Den Blå Krans excludes fragrance allergens and specific preservatives. Both restrict substances that are entirely legal. If the legal floor were where consumers wanted it, a label whose whole value proposition is *we removed things the law permits* would have no market. It has a large one, and it has had for decades. That is evidence about the floor rather than about the label. *The fair objection, and the reason this is not conclusive.* Ecolabels also sell reassurance, distinction and brand, so their existence alone does not prove the floor is too low. What makes the argument more than commercial is *which* substances they exclude: the additions cluster on persistence, allergenicity and endocrine activity — the three places where the risk-based assessment above is weakest, because all three do their damage at doses and over timescales that an exposure estimate handles badly</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-PG-OLD-ECOLABEL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** The labels' criteria, what they exclude, that what they exclude is legal, and the size of their market were in no source read; the sources read say only that the labels exist.

**Not replaced** — nothing that could be justified was found to say in its place.

`C-PG-OLD-F2` · retired 2026-09-11 from [PROGRAMME.md](PROGRAMME.md) · as published in `7954022`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-PG-OLD-F2">The deciding number is usable as a sign and not as a coefficient. *Markoverskud* — the field surplus that drives the model — fell [40](SOURCES.md#F-a971026358)–[53](SOURCES.md#F-bdd0e0f5a4)% across ten studied catchments. The measured diffuse load fell by [10](SOURCES.md#F-25d5541c87)–[14](SOURCES.md#F-fa5f83bb55) kg N/ha where the surplus fell [30](SOURCES.md#F-003df98ab8)–[52](SOURCES.md#F-9bd389ef17), by [3](SOURCES.md#F-dda14dbafe)–[5](SOURCES.md#F-5155d1b540) where it fell [24](SOURCES.md#F-2e7435d8f3)–[50](SOURCES.md#F-a4e9e62af8), and at Mariager by nothing at all. Pass-through runs from zero to about a third. A load reduction predicted from a surplus reduction is overestimated threefold to tenfold, or entirely. *Does not establish:* that the decline was not real. Measured estuary nitrogen fell [24](SOURCES.md#F-2e7435d8f3)–[62](SOURCES.md#F-f38b862051)% over the same period</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-PG-OLD-F2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

`C-PG-OLD-PMT` · retired 2026-09-11 from [PROGRAMME.md](PROGRAMME.md) · as published in `7954022`

## RESIDUAL.md

<a id="C-LR-OLD-AGREED"></a>
### A person and an algorithm agreed: the human-placed sheets moved by a fraction of their standard errors in the joint solution.

`C-LR-OLD-AGREED` · retired 2026-09-11 from [RESIDUAL.md](RESIDUAL.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-LR-OLD-AGREED">A person and an algorithm agreed. Some sheets were placed by a resident clicking landmarks on a web map. Others were placed by correlating one sheet's photographed ground against its neighbour's, by FFT. When all seven were solved together, the human-placed sheets moved by [0.2](SOURCES.md#F-2815320913) to [1.8](SOURCES.md#F-ca5f136099) standard errors — and the one that moved furthest was the sheet whose two control points sat at nearly the same height, so its north–south position was known in advance to be the weak one. The method corrected the axis that was already understood to be unconstrained. A tired person clicking and a cross-correlation fail in entirely unrelated ways, and they landed in the same place</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-LR-OLD-AGREED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Its justification was not recorded properly: how far each sheet moved was recorded only in a commit message; the alignment file that held it was never committed.

**Replaced by:** [`C-LR-R-SOLVED`](CLAIMS.md#C-LR-R-SOLVED) — each opens what it rests on.

<a id="C-LR-OLD-CLOTHES"></a>
### Descriptions of the output gap, NAIRU, excess mortality, attributable fraction and safety factors, with claims about interest rates, negative values and typical factors.

`C-LR-OLD-CLOTHES` · retired 2026-09-11 from [RESIDUAL.md](RESIDUAL.md) · as published in `4469fc7`

> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-LR-OLD-CLOTHES">The second quantity is unobservable. The gap is a residual, and interest rates are set with reference to it. - NAIRU — the unemployment rate below which inflation is said to accelerate. Not measurable. Backed out of other quantities. - Excess mortality — actual deaths minus the deaths a model says you should have expected. Sound and widely useful; also a difference between large numbers, and it routinely goes negative. - Attributable fraction in epidemiology — the share of cases said to be caused by an exposure. Computed from modelled risks, then reported as a count of people. - Safety factors in toxicology — the [10](SOURCES.md#F-216d17c8bb)s and [100](SOURCES.md#F-78a6fc0518)s dividing an observed dose to reach a permitted one. Deliberate, disclosed, defensible engineering judgements. Also constants someone chose, which then propagate through everything downstream as if measured</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](ARCHIVE.md#C-LR-OLD-CLOTHES "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Why it was retired:** Several parts had no source: that interest rates are set with reference to the output gap, that excess mortality routinely goes negative, that attributable fractions are reported as counts of people, and the typical sizes of safety factors. The definitions that could be pinned are kept.

**Replaced by:** [`C-LR-R-OUTPUTGAP`](CLAIMS.md#C-LR-R-OUTPUTGAP), [`C-LR-R-NAIRU`](CLAIMS.md#C-LR-R-NAIRU), [`C-LR-R-EXCESS`](CLAIMS.md#C-LR-R-EXCESS), [`C-LR-R-PAF`](CLAIMS.md#C-LR-R-PAF), [`C-LR-R-SAFETY`](CLAIMS.md#C-LR-R-SAFETY) — each opens what it rests on.
